newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana bourse ends week higher, bonds in favour.
newsitem.headline: Ghana bourse ends week higher, bonds in favour.

text.p: The Ghana Stock Exchange ended the week slightly higher on Friday with local investors, seeking a quick return on their investment, still opting for bonds rather than shares, dealers said.
The Ghana Stock Exchange All-Share index rose 0.16 points to close at 358.96, the exchange's market report showed. It closed the previous week on 358.11 points.
Monday's session was the second quietest of the year with just 4,210 shares changing hands.

Wednesday saw 28,584,950 shares traded. Social Security Bank (+50 cedis to 1,250 cedis) accounted for 28,507,200 of them after an international consortium of investment institutions bought a strategic 40 percent stake in the bank.
Enterprise Insurance Company (+3 cedis to 475 cedis) and consumer products company Unilever (+2 to 770) were the only risers on Friday. There were no fallers.
Offers outpaced bids on Friday by 667,180 to 235,670.
One dealer said on Wednesday that foreign investors hold up to 75 percent of shares on the exchange and were keeping the market going.

Ghanaians, he said, were showing greater interest in money market instruments offered as part of government strategy to curb inflation. "Money market instruments offer more attractive returns and Ghanaians are interested in having quick returns on their investments."
